newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine May jobless to fall one point - Fernandez.
newsitem.headline: Argentine May jobless to fall one point - Fernandez.

text.p: Argentina's next unemployment survey, to be conducted in May, will show the jobless rate falling at least one percentage point from the 17.3 percent registered last October, Economy Minister Roque Fernandez said in an interview published Monday.
"We have very strong expectations that May will show an important break in unemployment," Fernandez told the financial daily Ambito Financiero. "The index will fall at least one point."

Fernandez said previously that labor reforms, decreed in December, could reduce unemployment by 3-4 percentage points this year. Howevever, the decrees were challenged in court and the government is negotiating an agreement with business groups and unions to make the labor market more flexible.

Reports published several weeks ago suggested the government would change its unemployment survey, saying it included among the jobless those Argentines who were unhappy in their current jobs and were looking for other work.
However, Fernandez said in the interview that officials will not change the poll at all.
He added that he doubted it would be possible to lower taxes this year despite a recent recovery in tax collection.
"It will be difficult to consider this before the last quarter of the year, although I don't expect that we could do something even in the last quarter," the minister told Ambito.
"We have to be sure that the recovery in collection is permanent and that will take the whole year."
